goal: Extract attribute/protocol/enforced-attribute responsibility out of Safelist into a new class to reduce the number of public methods on Safelist and concentrate attribute-related logic into a cohesive responsibility class.

expected_impact.rationale: Eight public Safelist methods that together implement attribute configuration and attribute validation (addAttributes, removeAttributes, addEnforcedAttribute, removeEnforcedAttribute, addProtocols, removeProtocols, isSafeAttribute, getEnforcedAttributes) are extracted to a single new class (SafelistAttributes). Supporting private helpers (getProtocolValue, isSafeProtocol) and the backing maps (attributes, enforcedAttributes, protocols) are moved as well. This reduces Safelist's public method count and concentrates attribute/configuration responsibilities in a cohesive class. Some small delegations inside Safelist (e.g., shouldAbsUrl remains as a package-private delegating wrapper) are retained to preserve package-level behavior.

ops.details: Create a new class org.jsoup.safety.SafelistAttributes that encapsulates the attribute-configuration and validation responsibility currently in Safelist. Move the following fields from Safelist into SafelistAttributes: attributes (Map<TagName, Set<AttributeKey>>), enforcedAttributes (Map<TagName, Map<AttributeKey, AttributeValue>>), protocols (Map<TagName, Map<AttributeKey, Set<Protocol>>>). Move these public methods into SafelistAttributes (preserving their behaviour): addAttributes(...), removeAttributes(...), addEnforcedAttribute(...), removeEnforcedAttribute(...), addProtocols(...), removeProtocols(...), isSafeAttribute(...), getEnforcedAttributes(...). Move supporting private helpers getProtocolValue(Element, Attribute) and isSafeProtocol(String, Set<Protocol>) into SafelistAttributes as private methods of the new class. Implement constructors for SafelistAttributes: a default constructor and a copy-constructor SafelistAttributes(SafelistAttributes copy) that performs the same deep-copy semantics as the original Safelist copy constructor did for the moved maps. Update Safelist to hold a new final field: private final SafelistAttributes attributesConfig; initialize it in both Safelist() and Safelist(Safelist) (the copy constructor should call new SafelistAttributes(copy.attributesConfig)). Update all internal Safelist usages (within the same file) that previously referenced moved fields/methods to call through attributesConfig (for example, factory methods in Safelist that used chained addAttributes/removeAttributes must be updated to use the new attributesConfig methods where appropriate). Leave preserveRelativeLinks and its public setter/getter in Safelist; keep the package-private shouldAbsUrl(String, String) in Safelist but implement it as a delegating call to attributesConfig.shouldAbsUrl(TagName.valueOf(...), AttributeKey.valueOf(...)) so package-level behavior remains unchanged for other package types. The nested typed classes (TagName, AttributeKey, AttributeValue, Protocol, TypedValue) remain in Safelist and are referenced from SafelistAttributes as Safelist.TagName, Safelist.AttributeKey, etc., relying on package access. Ensure necessary imports (Element, Attribute, Attributes, Map, Set, HashMap, HashSet, Iterator, Objects, org.jsoup.internal.Normalizer static lowerCase) are present in the new class. The extraction preserves behavior; public Safelist methods moved to the new class are removed from Safelist. All internal call sites inside Safelist are updated to the new structure.

Update related tests affected by this refactoring block so the configured build command passes. Adjust imports, package references, moved class references, constructors, and assertions only when required. Do not change production behavior through tests.
